To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a coupling model was developed for the SS drying of compact distillers’ wet spent grain pellets with a thin layer (10–30%) of solubles coating.

a computational model for superheated steam (SHS) drying of multilayers can be developed by combining the mass and energy conservation equations for SHS and the diffusion equations for the coated pellet.
the developed 3D computational model can be used as a predictive tool to design and optimise the SS drying of coated distillers’ grains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational model that can be used for design of SS drying units.
the modelling of SS drying, a novel technology that can potentially improve drying efficiency and reduce energy consumption.
developing an effective approach for drying of wet spent grain by SS and developing a model for predicting the heat and mass transfer phenomenon of such drying.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study is the first to report the modelling of SS drying for multilayered materials.
the developed 3D CFD model is capable of predicting heat, and mass transfer phenomena in SS drying of coated pellets.
SS drying of compact distillers’ grains coated with soluble can be a potential solution for drying of slurry-like materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed 3D model can be used to simulate SS drying of multicomponent materials and can be used for design and optimization of industrial SS drying units.
the developed 3D model is capable of accurately predicting the SS drying process of multilayer coated spent grain pellets.
SS is a promising drying medium for multilayered product and a 3D modelling approach can be used to predict SS drying of such materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of superheated drying for the drying of wet materials can be a viable alternative to hot air drying.
SS drying of compact distillers’ grains with solubles can reduce the energy consumption and drying time by 20 and 40% compared to the hot air drying, respectively.
SS drying of coated distillers spent grains can be a potential solution for the large-scale drying of spent grains.
